description: Trigger: caller invokes calendar_set or participant_identity_set with a create map. Calendar.id (crate-jmap-calendars-types/src/calendar.rs:106) and ParticipantIdentity.id (crate-jmap-calendars-types/src/participant_identity.rs:19) are typed as required (non-Option) Id and lack skip_serializing_if. The typed create-map values therefore force callers to construct objects carrying an id and the JSON serializer emits id:"<placeholder>" on the wire inside each create-map value. Per RFC 8620 §5.3, id MUST NOT be set by the client on creation — the server assigns the id and either ignores or rejects a client-supplied id (jmapd-class servers may treat any leading '#' as a creationId reference). Bad behavior: malformed wire payload that depends on server tolerance; non-tolerant servers reject the request with invalidProperties. CalendarEvent.id is correctly Option<Id> + skip_serializing_if (event.rs:43-44), so calendar_event_set is fine. The existing smoke test tests/participant_identity_smoke_tests.rs::participant_identity_set_create_round_trip sets id:"placeholder" and the assertion does NOT check that id is absent from the wire create map — the test is too weak to catch this. Fix is in jmap-calendars-types (make id Option<Id> with skip_serializing_if on Calendar and ParticipantIdentity to match CalendarEvent), but the client-side test should also assert id absence on the wire create-map values.
title: calendar_set / participant_identity_set create map serializes required id field on the wire violating RFC 8620 §5.3
